paper_title: Search for ultralight axion dark matter in a side-band analysis of a 199Hg free-spin precession signal
suggested_experiment_name: PSI-HgM-sideband (PSI 199Hg free-spin precession with sideband analysis)
coupling_convention: g_NN in GeV^-1 (axion-nucleon coupling constant, plotted directly from Figure 4)
notes: This is a null-result exclusion limit from a 199Hg free-spin precession magnetometer search for ultralight axion dark matter via the axion-wind effect. The paper reports a peak sensitivity of g_aNN ≈ 3.5 × 10^-6 GeV^-1 over the mass range 10^-16 eV ≲ m_a ≲ 10^-13 eV (corresponding to Compton frequencies f_a ≲ 21.4 Hz). The coupling is to nucleon spins; the 199Hg system is predominantly sensitive to axion-neutron coupling (g_aN) with ~10× weaker dependence on axion-proton coupling (g_aP). The limit assumes equal coupling to neutrons and protons (g_aNN = g_aN + g_aP). The DM density assumption ρ_DM = 0.4 GeV/cm³ is the lower conservative bound of the 2σ range [0.4–0.8 GeV/cm³]. Data extracted from abstract and Figure 4. The coupling value 3.5 × 10^-6 GeV^-1 is stated in the abstract as the peak sensitivity; this is a mass-independent bound valid across the stated mass range, encoded as a horizontal line. The paper uses Lomb-Scargle periodogram analysis of 297 free-spin-precession signals (100 s each, ~13 hours total) to search for frequency modulation sidebands at ω_a ± ω_Hg.
